correctness.rationale: The exact scalar hypergradient update simplifies to projection of x/(ax+B). Inside the invariant basin |ax|<b_min, an opposite-sign noise draw resets the stepsize to zero, and two repetitions of a same-sign atom then hit the minimizer exactly. Conditioning on disjoint three-step blocks gives the stated geometric tail and expectation bound.

originality.rationale: The current OSGM-SGD source explicitly leaves non-vanishing gradient noise as an open direction. Targeted searches found no prior OSGM-SGD result with this discrete reset-and-hit mechanism. Known finite-time persistent-noise results for stochastic mirror descent require sharp minima and do not cover a smooth quadratic minimum.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a rigorous positive special case for a recent open OSGM-SGD direction, an explicit geometric hitting-time bound, and a finite-sum corollary, while explaining why adaptive exact-function feedback can eliminate a noise floor that remains for constant-step SGD.
